text:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming SLO breach detected (service=/v1/stream/generate, region=us-west-2). p99 > 3s for 6 consecutive 1m windows. Auto-page to oncall group. :bangbang:

Priya: ACK — I'm oncall. jumping in. tagging @Derek and @Hui for infra/hardware.

Derek: seeing p95 ~ 850ms but p99 has a long tail ~3.8-5.2s. Metrics show spike aligns with queue depth increases on stream-frontend pods in AZ-b.

Hui: fetching node metrics. Running:
```
ssh gpu-node-23
nvidia-smi -q | egrep "ECC|Temperature"
sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --since "30 minutes ago" | tail -n 80
```

Hui: quick summary: GPU index 3 on node-23 has repeated "Corrected ECC" entries. temp readings: stabilized ~90C before the page, now 86C. fan at 98%. Kernel showing repeated soft errors and brief driver resets (no full panic).

Priya: ok that points to hardware-level correctables causing transient RPC stalls. Rafael, can you take traffic actions: move high-priority tenants to warm pool + enable fallback smaller model? Also can we temporarily reduce streaming batch windows?

Rafael: doing routing changes now. Commands I applied: `trafficctl override --route streaming --tenants high-prio --to warm-pool-us-east-1` and lowered batch window for stream route from 50ms -> 25ms. Warm-pool scaled by +1 replica.

ops-bot: cluster-autoscaler: launched 1 additional GPU node in us-west-2 (node-27).

Derek: initiating node isolation: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-23 && kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 12 pods evicted. Noting some cold starts and a few 5xx from modelcache misses.

Priya: monitoring tail. p99 dropped to 1.9s within 4 minutes after drain+reroute. p95 stable ~700ms. Still seeing intermittent streaming stalls (~1 every 3-5 minutes).

Hui: I pulled dmesg snippets: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): Corrected ECC error, type 2" repeated. BIOS telemetry shows fan curve responded but temps hit sustained high. Suggest thermal throttling or marginal VRAM module.

Derek: ran memtest-image on node-23 in maintenance container: found sporadic correctable errors under sustained alloc+write workload. Will schedule full offline memtest and powercycle.

Priya: customer impact quick note: window 16:42-16:51 UTC. Affected: 9 tenants saw increased retries/timeouts. Highest affected: BetaLabs (approx 210 streaming failures), internal monitoring triggered pager. No evidence of model output corruption.

Rafael: support communication queued: draft to BetaLabs summarizing transient latency spike, mention fallback routing and that weve isolated a degraded GPU node. Will offer post-incident call.

Hui: temp mitigation attempt: reduced GPU clock throttle via nvidia-smi persistence (lowered power cap by 10%) to reduce thermal output. Temps dropped to 78C after 6m; correctable error rate slowed but not stopped.

Priya: good. let's keep node drained; Rafael keep routing override for high-SLO tenants for 30m or until p99 < 1.2s for 20m. Derek please open a hardware ticket (RMA) for GPU slot AF:03 on node-23 and mark node as degraded in inventory.

Derek: RMA ticket created: HW-7732. Also set node annotation `redwood/health=degraded` and scheduled overnight powercycle + extended memtest.

ops-bot: action: added automated drain policy to run if correctables > 50 within 10m (PR: infra/alerts#402).

Priya: follow-ups: 1) update runbook to include traffic reroute step (fast path) 2) add alert smoothing to avoid noisy single-window pages 3) consider adding a KV-cache circuit-breaker for streaming path to reduce stalls from memory-correctable bursts.

support-bot: support ticket INC-2598 opened and assigned to Support with SLA urgency: high.

Priya: timeline + summary for postmortem: root cause likely marginal GPU module producing high rate of correctable ECC events under load; this caused driver-level retries and stalls in streaming KV-cache path, amplifying tail latency. Mitigations applied: node cordon+drain, scaled warm pool, routing override for high-SLO tenants, lowered batch window, temporary GPU power cap. Impact window and counts above. Action items: RMA, memtest, add auto-drain policy, update runbook, customer comms.

Rafael: leaving routing override in place until 17:30 UTC or until p99 stable.

Priya: handing off post-incident ownership to Derek for hardware follow-ups and to Rafael for customer comms. My oncall ends at 17:00 UTC.

Derek: taking hardware owner. Will upload logs to s3://redwood-incidents/2218765432/node-23/ and prepare postmortem draft.

Priya: closing alert in channel. Leaving thread for docs. :white_check_mark:
